action.thought:
Let me design the erasure feature based on what I've learned about the codebase.

## Architecture understanding
- Multi-service architecture: api-gateway (proxies), customer-service (customers, addresses, contacts, payment methods, support tickets), payment-service (payments, refunds, invoices, provider sandbox), document-worker (receipts via jobs), notification-worker (emails via kafka events), projection-worker (search/redis via kafka events), webhook-worker (provider webhooks).
- Postgres schemas: platform, customers, payments, operations, provider_sandbox.
- Customer PII lives in:
  - customers.customers (email, name, phone, external_reference, metadata)
  - customers.addresses (line1, line2, city, region, postal_code, country)
  - customers.contacts (value - email/phone)
  - customers.payment_method_refs (provider_token, billing_name, billing_address, last4, brand)
  - customers.support_messages (body - may contain PII), customers.support_tickets/support_participants
  - customers.customer_imports + operations.document_manifests (object_key points to MinIO - customer_import object has content in MinIO with full record)
  - customers.provider_customer_mappings (provider_customer_id - not PII itself but links)
  - provider_sandbox.customers (email, name, external_reference) - this is "provider side" customer profile, mirrors payflow customer info, must also be erased since it's PayFlow-controlled sandbox provider (simulates a real provider that PayFlow's own mock-processor controls - but is it merchant's own system?). The provider_sandbox schema is used by the mock payment processor (payment-service manages payment-intents which POST to PROCESSOR_URL which is itself the payment-service, i.e mock-processor is same service). This is "PayFlow-controlled" since it's in the same Postgres DB, same service scope. So must be erased too, but it's not a financial record (it's provider's copy for sandbox purposes) - so we should scrub email/name here too, OR delete since it doesn't have accounting need. Actually provider_sandbox.customers just tracks the provider's view of the customer info - required for future payment operations at provider. If deleted, future operations for that customer would break (but customer deletion should mean no more payment attempts). We should just scrub PII fields (email, name, external_reference) to anonymized values, keeping the row for referential integrity (payment_intents.provider_customer_id references... wait no FK, but there's a table `provider_sandbox.payment_intents.provider_customer_id` and captures don't reference customer directly). We could just delete provider_sandbox.customers row since nothing references it via FK from other rows (check: provider_customer_mappings has FK on customer_id customers.customers(id) but this is separate to provider_sandbot.customers). Let's check if anything references provider_sandbox.customers(id) via FK - searching.

- payments.payment_intents.customer_snapshot jsonb (denormalized customer at time of payment - name/email/phone) - MUST retain financial correctness but no longer identify customer. Also customer_id column (uuid) - keep as pointer since financial record needs to link but "no longer identify the deleted customer" - the requirement says financial records must remain financially correct but not identify the customer. The customer_id itself is an internal UUID; is it "identifying"? Probably the customer_id linking to a soft-deleted customer row (whose PII has been erased) is fine, since it's an opaque identifier that no longer points to any personal data. That satisfies "no longer identify the deleted customer" - as long as looking up customer_id after erasure yields no personal info (customer row scrubbed but still exists as tombstone). Actually maybe simplest: keep customer_id (FK-like, not actual FK based on schema) pointing to customers.customers.id, and scrub customers.customers row's PII fields (email/name/phone/metadata) but keep id/merchant_id/status='erased' and external_reference tombstoned. Then customer_snapshot JSON (frozen at payment time) must also be scrubbed since it contains name/email/phone directly - and it's a copy, so scrubbing the live customer row doesn't automatically remove old snapshots! We need to actively update all payment_intents.customer_snapshot for erased customer, replacing PII with tombstone while preserving non-PII financial shape.

- payments.refunds.customer_email - directly contains email; must scrub.
- payments.invoices.billing_snapshot jsonb (contains full customer object from customer-service GET including email, name, phone, addresses maybe) - must scrub PII fields but retain financial totals/currency etc.
- payments.invoices object_key -> MinIO stored invoice JSON document containing full customer echo - stored object contains PII in object storage ("actively stores... personal data" - MinIO documents are actively exposed). Need to remove/scrub the invoice document object in MinIO, or replace with redacted version, since retrieval of that document would expose PII. But invoice needs to remain available for financial history - "Retained records must preserve their financial meaning while no longer identifying the deleted customer." So the invoice document (PDF/JSON) needs to be regenerated w/o PII, or deleted from MinIO since it's not required for financial correctness per se (the DB row with totals is the "record"). Simplify: delete/redact stored object content (overwrite with redacted version) and keep manifest referencing it, OR simply delete the file since it's a rendering, not the ledger fact. I think safest: redact the object content in place (overwrite the object key with a version containing no PII, preserving totals/currency/lines), so any future generation of a "reprint" won't include PII, and existing references (object_key) remain valid but content is scrubbed.

- operations.document_manifests.customer_id - can keep as pointer (opaque link), no PII stored directly in this table besides metadata jsonb which for receipts contains {paymentId}, for invoices contains {invoiceId, number} - no PII. For customer_import manifests: metadata = {importId, source} - no direct PII. OK fine.

- customers.customer_imports doesn't store PII directly in DB (content is in MinIO object). The MinIO object for customer_imports (`${merchantId}/imports/${importId}.json`) contains raw imported record dumped from generate-scenario or importCustomerArtifact - typically contains email/phone/notes. This is "customer data actively stored" and is not a financial record (not payment-related, just an import history document) - must be deleted. So we should delete these objects from MinIO entirely (not financial).

- Receipts (document-worker generated `${merchantId}/receipts/${paymentId}.json`) - contains customerSnapshot (name/email/phone) + amount, currency, issuedAt. This is a receipt = financial record type (payment history)? The doc says "retain financial facts needed for payment history, refunds, reconciliation, and accounting" — receipts probably count as needed for payment history/accounting. But similar to invoice, must no longer identify customer. So we should redact receipts in MinIO too (replace customer field with anonymized placeholder), keeping amount/currency/paymentId/issuedAt.

- support_tickets/support_messages: subject/body could contain PII (message content), and support_participants links ticket to customer_id. This is NOT financial - so should be deleted entirely (support tickets aren't listed as retained categories: "payments, invoices, ledger entries" only). We should delete customer's support messages & participant links entirely (and maybe tickets if solely owned by this customer, but tickets might have multiple participants... in our schema each support_ticket created via createSupportTicket auto adds a single support_participant), we can delete messages by customer + delete participant row; if ticket has no more participants, could delete ticket & messages entirely. Given complexity, simplest robust approach: delete all support_messages authored by customer (author_id=customer, author_type='customer'), delete support_participants row, and delete the ticket itself if no other participants remain (since currently 1 participant per ticket only ever created). That fully removes customer's data without affecting others.

- customers.payment_method_refs: providerToken, billing_name, billing_address, brand, last4 - all tied to customer_id NOT NULL REFERENCES customers.customers(id). action.message:
I implemented customer data deletion (erasure) for PayFlow per `docs/privacy-api.md` and `docs/privacy-and-retention.md`, and validated it end-to-end against the full local stack (Postgres, Redis, Kafka/Redpanda, MinIO, OpenSearch, Mailpit).

## API (customer-service, proxied by api-gateway)
- `POST /v1/customers/:customerId/erasure-requests` — requires `privacy:erase` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header (8–200 chars). Returns `202` with `{id, customerId, status, attempts, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, lastError}`.
  - Same key + same customer → returns the same saved request (replay).
  - Same key + different customer → `409`.
  - Different key + a customer that already has a request → returns the existing request instead of starting a second workflow.
  - Unknown customer or customer belonging to another merchant → `404`, no side effects (the whole check happens inside one transaction that rolls back on 404).
- `GET /v1/erasure-requests/:requestId` — requires `privacy:erase` scope, `404` if missing or owned by another merchant.
- Gateway route `/v1/erasure-requests` added so the GET endpoint is reachable publicly.

## Async erasure worker
Runs inside `customer-service` (alongside the existing outbox publisher), using the same lease/claim/retry pattern as the other background workers in the codebase (`customers.erasure_requests` table with `locked_by`/`lease_expires_at`, exponential backoff, automatic lease recovery after a crash). Every step is idempotent so retries/resumes converge without redoing destructive work — verified by killing OpenSearch mid-run and watching the request fail with a stable, non-PII error code, keep retrying, and complete automatically once the dependency came back, without re-running the already-committed DB scrub.

## What gets erased vs. retained
- **Deleted** (not financial): addresses, contacts, payment method refs, support tickets/messages, provider-customer mappings, notification preferences/emails/deliveries.
- **Tombstoned**: the customer row itself (email/name/phone/external_reference/metadata replaced, `status='erased'`, `erased_at` set) — deterministic values so retries are safe.
- **Retained but redacted** (financial correctness preserved): `payment_intents.customer_snapshot`, `refunds.customer_email`, `invoices.billing_snapshot`, `analytics_events`; amounts/currency/status/ids are untouched.
- **Redacted in place**: MinIO-stored receipt/invoice JSON documents (verified byte-for-byte that totals/currency/lines survive while customer fields are replaced), plus removal of the customer's Redis cache entry and OpenSearch document.
- **Protects delayed/replayed work**: pending `operations.jobs` and not-yet-published `operations.outbox_events` payloads referencing the customer are redacted during erasure; `notification-worker` and `projection-worker` additionally check `status='erased'` before writing any PII, so already-queued or replayed events can't resurrect data after erasure completes.

## Supporting changes
- Migration `009_privacy_erasure.sql` (erasure_requests table + `customers.erased_at`).
- New shared `packages/http/src/idempotency.ts` and `packages/operations/src/pii-redaction.ts` (unit-tested).
- `scripts/seed.ts` grants the new `privacy:erase` scope to seeded API keys.
- `scripts/check-runtime.ts` updated so it distinguishes active vs. erased customers when checking Redis/OpenSearch projection completeness.
- Fixed a pre-existing `mailpit` healthcheck bug in `docker-compose.yml` (busybox `wget` was being routed through the sandbox's proxy) that was blocking local startup.

## Verification performed
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` all pass (added `tests/privacy.test.ts` for the redaction helper).
- Full docker-compose stack brought up from scratch; ran `npm run migrate`, `seed`, `scenario`, `smoke`, `provider:check`, and `runtime-check` — all green, including ledger balance and zero dead letters.
- Scripted end-to-end erasure test: created a customer with addresses/contacts/payment method/support ticket, ran a real payment + invoice through the sandbox, then erased the customer and confirmed every one of the behaviors above via direct DB/Redis/OpenSearch/MinIO inspection, plus idempotency-key edge cases (400 on bad key, 401 without auth, 404s, replay/cross-customer/cross-tenant behavior).

No other public API contracts were changed. Everything was tested only inside the supplied repo/environment.
